nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The developer/orchestrator who runs the recovery CLIs (es-merge, es-generate, demo) and launches es-view. Here they invoke es-generate to render a validated flows.json into the two shipped, openable views.

nodes.label: GenerateViews
nodes.description: Render the canonical flows.json into the two shipped views: a Graphviz flows.dot digraph (one cluster per flow, event-storming palette) and a single self-contained explorer.html with the whole model inlined. A deterministic, stateless projection: it reads the model and writes two files, mutating nothing.

tactical.explanation: Entry tools/generate-views.js (the es-generate bin). Guards argv: missing <flows.json> or <outDir> prints usage and exits 2 (22). It then JSON.parses the flows file into `model` with NO try/catch and NO validation (24) -- it fully trusts es-merge's output contract. repoRoot/title resolve from --repo-root/--title, falling back to model.meta.repoRoot/title then './'Event Storming Explorer' (27-28). It indexes nodeById / hotspotById (30-31) and a DATA_TYPES filter that excludes datastore/field nodes and any edge touching them from the board + DOT (36-37). DOT pass: one `subgraph cluster_<flowid>` per flow, sticky per used node colored by PALETTE, dead flows dashed + greyed, node label URL='vscode://file/<repoRoot>/<path>:<line>' from the first anchor; written to <outDir>/flows.dot (60-89). HTML pass: the model is serialized with JSON.stringify(model).replace(/</g,'\u003c') (92, the one injection guard) and inlined as `const MODEL` alongside REPO_ROOT + PALETTE (436-438) into a ~1400-line self-contained template (tabs: Flows, Gallery, Data model, Glossary, Overview); written to <outDir>/explorer.html (1519). Two sequential writeFileSync calls to the same outDir; no mkdir (outDir must pre-exist).

anchors.note: argv guard: missing flows/outDir => usage + exit 2
JSON.parse(readFileSync(flowsFile)) -- no try/catch, no validation
writeFileSync(outDir/flows.dot, dot.join)
modelJson = JSON.stringify(model).replace(/</g,'\u003c') -- HTML injection guard
writeFileSync(outDir/explorer.html, html)

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): deduped nodes plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. In THIS flow it is a READ-ONLY input -- the generator projects it into views and never mutates or re-validates it. Its invariants are enforced upstream at merge time, not here.

tactical.explanation: generate-views.js JSON.parses flows.json into `model` (24) and builds nodeById / hotspotById indexes (30-31) plus the DATA_TYPES exclusion filter (36-37). It reads model.meta.repoRoot / model.meta.title as fallbacks for the --repo-root / --title flags (27-28) and model.nodes / model.flows / model.hotspots throughout the DOT and HTML passes. The generator performs NO validation of its own -- it assumes the aggregate's merge-time invariants already held (see hot-generator-trusts-unvalidated-model).

anchors.note: model = JSON.parse(readFileSync(flowsFile))
nodeById / hotspotById indexes over model.nodes / model.hotspots

nodes.label: Graphviz flows.dot
nodes.description: The Graphviz digraph the operator renders offline (e.g. `dot -Tsvg model/flows.dot`) or opens in a Graphviz viewer to read the whole board at a glance: one clustered subgraph per flow, event-storming-colored stickies, labeled edges, dead flows dashed and greyed. Physical storage nodes (datastore/field) and any edge touching them are deliberately excluded so the DOT stays behavioral.

tactical.explanation: Built by the DOT pass (60-88) and written to <outDir>/flows.dot (89). Per flow it emits `subgraph cluster_<flowid>`, computes the `used` node set from steps + edges while skipping data-type ids via isDataId (70-72), and for each used node emits a filled/rounded box colored by PALETTE[type] with fontcolor = the palette's tonal text, a truncated description tooltip, and URL='vscode://file/<repoRoot>/<firstAnchor.path>:<line>' so a Graphviz SVG's nodes deep-link into the local checkout (73-84). Node ids are namespaced `<flowid>__<nodeid>` so a shared node appears once per flow cluster. Edges whose endpoints survived the data filter are drawn with the verb as label (82-85).

anchors.note: DOT digraph header + per-flow cluster loop
used-node set excludes datastore/field via isDataId
writeFileSync(outDir/flows.dot)

nodes.label: Interactive explorer.html
nodes.description: The self-contained, no-server interactive explorer the operator opens in a browser: the whole model is inlined as a JS constant and rendered into five tabs (Flows board, Gallery of every sticky, Data model, Glossary, Overview) with a sticky-lane board, detail panel, search, group-by pivots, and vscode:// deep links to the analyzed source. This is the primary artifact the recovery produces.

tactical.explanation: The whole `model` is serialized once (JSON.stringify(model).replace(/</g,'\u003c') to neutralize </script> injection, 92) and inlined as `const MODEL` with REPO_ROOT + PALETTE (436-438) into a ~1400-line HTML/CSS/vanilla-JS template (94-1518), written to <outDir>/explorer.html (1519). No external dependencies are referenced -- the page is fully offline. Client anchors render as `vscode://file/<REPO_ROOT>/<path>:<line>` links (476) that open the analyzed checkout in VS Code. The client-side rendering (sidebar grouping, board layout, gallery, glossary, data-model tab) is the same projection logic later ported into the React SPA under src/web/*; here it is baked statically into one file.

anchors.note: modelJson escaped for safe inlining into the HTML
MODEL / REPO_ROOT / PALETTE inlined into the page
writeFileSync(outDir/explorer.html, html)

nodes.label: Web browser
nodes.description: The operator's browser, which opens the self-contained explorer.html directly from disk (no server). It renders the inlined model and drives all interaction; outside the tool's deploy boundary.

nodes.label: VS Code
nodes.description: The local editor targeted by the vscode://file/<repoRoot>/<path>:<line> deep links baked into both flows.dot node URLs and the explorer.html anchors. Clicking a recovered concept opens the exact source line in the analyzed checkout. Outside the tool's boundary.

nodes.label: Graphviz (dot)
nodes.description: The external Graphviz `dot` renderer the operator runs over flows.dot (e.g. `dot -Tsvg`) to produce a static image of the whole board. Not bundled; the generator only emits the .dot source.

tactical.explanation: generate-views writes DOT source only; rendering is an out-of-process step the operator invokes (documented in the example README as `dot -Tsvg model/flows.dot -o flows.svg`). The emitted node URLs survive into a Graphviz SVG as clickable vscode:// links.

anchors.note: digraph header written for the dot renderer

nodes.label: Local filesystem
nodes.description: The local filesystem reached through node:fs. Here it holds the input flows.json read by the generator and receives the two output view files written into outDir.

tactical.explanation: Accessed via require('fs'): readFileSync(flowsFile) reads the input model; writeFileSync writes <outDir>/flows.dot and <outDir>/explorer.html. No mkdir is performed, so outDir must already exist.

anchors.note: const fs = require('fs') -- the filesystem boundary

nodes.label: flows.json (canonical model)
nodes.description: The canonical model file. Written by es-merge; consumed here as the read-only input of es-generate. Between the two CLIs (separate node processes) this on-disk file IS the hand-off store.

tactical.explanation: generate-views.js reads it with fs.readFileSync(flowsFile,'utf8') and JSON.parses it into `model` (24); it is never written by this flow.

anchors.note: readFileSync(flowsFile) -> JSON.parse

nodes.label: flows.dot (Graphviz digraph)
nodes.description: Output file: the Graphviz DOT source for the whole board, one cluster per flow. Written into outDir. Backing store for the rm-flows-dot read model.

tactical.explanation: Serialized as dot.join('\n') and written with fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir,'flows.dot'), ...) at the end of the DOT pass.

anchors.note: writeFileSync(outDir/flows.dot)

nodes.label: explorer.html (self-contained SPA)
nodes.description: Output file: the single self-contained interactive explorer with the whole model inlined. Written into outDir. Backing store for the rm-explorer-html read model.

tactical.explanation: The assembled HTML template string is written with fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir,'explorer.html'), html) as the last IO step; a success line then prints flow/node/hotspot counts.

anchors.note: writeFileSync(outDir/explorer.html, html)

flows.name: Operator generates the DOT + explorer views from the validated model
flows.summary: The operator runs es-generate (or the demo wrapper) over a validated flows.json and an output directory. The tool JSON.parses the model, then in one deterministic pass renders two artifacts: a Graphviz flows.dot digraph (one event-storming-colored cluster per flow, physical datastore/field nodes excluded) and a single self-contained explorer.html with the whole model inlined and no external dependencies. Both are written into outDir; the operator opens explorer.html in a browser and can render flows.dot with Graphviz, with vscode:// deep links from either back into the analyzed source. The generator is a pure projection: it reads the model read-only, enforces none of the model's invariants, and trusts that es-merge already validated the input.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `node tools/generate-views.js <flows.json> <outDir> [--repo-root <path>] [--title <text>]` (the `es-generate` bin), or `npm run demo` chains it after es-merge (scripts/build-example.mjs:14).

hotspots.label: es-generate renders any flows.json without validating it
hotspots.description: generate-views.js JSON.parses flows.json and immediately indexes model.nodes / model.hotspots / model.flows with no validation and no try/catch. Unlike the server's resolve-model.mjs (which re-runs the merge and throws on errors), the es-generate CLI performs zero checks. Combined with the merge writing flows.json even when validation fails (see hot-invalid-model-written), an operator can es-generate an invalid or partial model and get a silently broken/misleading explorer, or a raw crash: a missing top-level array (nodes/hotspots) throws an uncaught TypeError from .map (30-31), and a missing outDir throws from writeFileSync (no mkdir). Human question: should es-generate re-validate its input (import mergeTraceDocs, or at least assert the required arrays) and fail loudly before rendering, or is trusting es-merge's output contract intended? Today the two consumers of flows.json disagree on whether to trust it.

tactical.explanation: tools/generate-views.js:24 `const model = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(flowsFile,'utf8'))` -- no try/catch, no schema check. Lines 30-31 `new Map(model.nodes.map(...))` / `new Map(model.hotspots.map(...))` assume those arrays exist; 1522 reads model.flows.length. No `require` of src/lib/merge.mjs anywhere in the file. Contrast src/server/resolve-model.mjs, which throws when merged.errors.length so the server never serves an unvalidated model. No fs.mkdirSync of outDir, so a non-existent output dir also throws from writeFileSync.

anchors.note: JSON.parse with no try/catch and no validation
model.nodes / model.hotspots .map assume the arrays exist
writeFileSync with no mkdir of outDir
